summary.headline: Advanced Enzyme Q2 FY27 revenue rose 16% YoY to INR2,145 million and EBITDA margin reached 34%, with management guiding 30-32% margins going forward.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q2 FY27 was INR2,145 million, up 16% YoY and 12% QoQ, while H1 revenue grew 10% to INR4,062 million. EBITDA rose 20% YoY to INR721 million (34% margin vs 33% a year ago and 28% in Q1), and PAT rose 14% YoY to INR512 million (24% margin). Management said deferred sales of about INR10 crore from Q1 were only partly recovered (INR2.5 crore net), with INR7.5 crore carried into the next quarter. Management urged investors to assess the business on an annual basis rather than quarterly.

segments.name: Human Healthcare
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,285 million, +6% YoY and +11% QoQ, driven by Pharma/API, Biocatalysis and Nutrition; flat on YTD basis. Biocatalysis within Human Healthcare was INR66 million in Q2 vs about INR45 million in Q1.

segments.name: Animal Healthcare
segments.commentary: Revenue INR265 million, +37% YoY, +5% QoQ and +14% YTD; about 12% of group revenue.

segments.name: Bio-Processing
segments.commentary: Revenue INR365 million, +43% YoY, +19% QoQ and +37% in H1; about 17% of group revenue.

segments.name: Specialized Manufacturing (SciTech)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR231 million (segment reported), +25% YoY, +15% QoQ, +32% in H1; subsidiary SciTech reported Q2 revenue INR234 million, EBITDA INR61 million and PAT INR36 million, with H1 EBITDA up 144% and PAT about 6x YoY.

segments.name: JC Biotech (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR200 million (vs INR186 million), EBITDA INR29 million (vs INR37 million), PAT INR17 million (flat); H1 revenue INR395 million vs INR397 million.

segments.name: Evoxx (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR75 million, EBITDA INR4 million, loss of INR7 million (vs loss of INR18 million in Q1 and PAT of INR14 million a year ago); H1 loss INR26 million vs INR21 million profit last year.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin guided at 30-32% on an overall basis for calculation purposes.
Management expects progressive momentum through the year and expects the U.S. market to pick up toward year-end, with a possible margin upside if it does.
Long-run growth intent is double digits, mid to lower-mid double digits; FY27 segment guidance to come after February-March budgeting.
Capex guidance for FY27 unchanged at about INR123 crore (including R&D and maintenance); about INR52 crore already spent in H1.
Human Healthcare Pharma/API expected to recover further toward year-end.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex guidance of about INR123 crore including R&D and maintenance; about INR52 crore spent in H1.
SciTech capacity utilisation rose with added shifts, improving efficiencies; the company did not give specific capacity figures.
R&D spend INR90 million in Q2 (vs INR86 million) and INR216 million in H1 (vs INR166 million); about 4.3% of consolidated revenue after intercompany elimination vs 3% in Q2 FY26.
demand_pricing: U.S. market described as dull for the first two quarters due to global conditions; management expects pick-up toward year-end, citing SupplySide West interest and new potential customers, with timing of one to two quarters.

Growth is coming from food, animal feed and Biocatalysis; management said it is adding new customers and geographies rather than relying on existing clients, and existing clients in the U.S. are not growing rapidly.
Top-10 customers were 26% of Q2 revenue (vs 27%) and 22% in H1 (vs 23%). B2C revenue was USD 0.91 million in H1 (vs USD 1.29 million).
New products and applications contributed about 7-8% of revenue, per management's approximate estimate.
Management said Novonesis's large capex in India is aimed at bioethanol, where Advanced Enzyme is not present; current revenue is not expected to be affected.

qa_highlights.question: Would underlying sales growth be 12-13% or 10-11% after adjusting for Q1 deferment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR10 crore was deferred in Q1, of which INR2.5 crore was recovered net and INR7.5 crore carried into next quarter; the target is lower double-digit growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving SciTech's margin and revenue scale-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth is broad-based, driven by added shifts, higher capacity utilisation, efficiency gains, a wider customer base and R&D projects now paying off.

qa_highlights.question: Employee cost fell from INR45 crore in Q1 to INR40 crore in Q2; what is the run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Drop attributed to a about INR1 crore provision reversal, ESOP cost reversal for departed employees, and lower U.S. headcount; management declined to fix a sustainable run rate as hiring continues.

qa_highlights.question: What is cash balance after the buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash was about INR640 crore at 30 September and about INR610 crore after roughly INR30 crore spent in October, excluding October accruals. Buyback: 2.41 million shares at average INR289.09.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Biocatalysis business trending and what is its size?
qa_highlights.answer: Biocatalysis within Human Healthcare was INR66 million in Q2 vs about INR45 million in Q1; management expects most Human Healthcare growth to come from it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of WELLFA, the B2C brand?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue is negligible; it has been separated into its own company, and management is not counting on material revenue for the next two to three years. It declined to give a 3-year revenue target of INR30-40 crore.

risks_watch: U.S. recovery timing: management has pointed to one to two quarters, but the U.S. has underperformed for several quarters.
Q1 deferred sales (about INR7.5 crore carried forward) must be recognised in Q3 to sustain growth.
Employee cost run rate uncertain after one-off reversals in Q2; hiring is ongoing.
Evoxx remains loss-making (H1 loss INR26 million).
Input costs for power, fuel and raw materials remained elevated, per management.
Dependence on the company's largest product, where competitor supply disruptions have helped; management declined to share product revenue.
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line momentum and margins, but cautious and non-committal on the U.S. timeline, quarterly run rate and segment guidance. Management repeatedly deflected specific numerical questions (product revenue, employee cost run rate, WELLFA targets) and asked investors to evaluate on an annual basis.
key_quotes: we always suggest all our shareholders to evaluate our business on an annual horizon rather than through the lens of a single quarter
we will continue as our guidelines, which we say that between 30% to 32% on an overall basis
But we expect it to pick up as we move on towards the year-end.

growth.why: Management reiterates long-run double-digit growth (mid to lower-mid double digits) and a 30-32% EBITDA margin for FY27, with capex held at about INR123 crore; backing is vague, relying on a US pick-up expected toward year-end and new customers/geographies, with no specific capacity or order numbers given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides 30-32% EBITDA margin for FY27 vs 34% achieved in Q2 and 28% in Q1, so guidance implies flat-to-lower margins, with upside only if the U.S. market recovers toward year-end.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 revenue grew 10% YoY to INR4,062 million and Q2 grew 16%, with management targeting lower double-digit growth and a U.S. pick-up toward year-end, but the U.S. was described as dull for two quarters and about INR7.5 crore of deferred sales carries into Q3.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex held at about INR123 crore with about INR52 crore spent in H1, and no capacity figures or new plant were disclosed, so no new capex announcement was signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held guidance (30-32% margin, double-digit growth) and cautioned against quarterly assessment, with H1 PAT up only 5% YoY, so no upgrade was signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: U.S. has underperformed for several quarters, management's recovery timing is one to two quarters, and input costs for power, fuel and raw materials remain elevated, so a shortfall versus the 'lower double-digit' target is possible.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: New products and applications already contribute about 7-8% of revenue and management is adding new customers and geographies, but no specific launch dates were given.

rows.label: Deferred sales recovery in Q3
rows.why: About INR7.5 crore of Q1 deferred sales carried into the next quarter, and management needs these recognised in Q3 to sustain growth.

rows.label: U.S. demand pick-up toward year-end
rows.why: Management cites SupplySide West interest and new potential customers with a one-to-two-quarter timeline, but U.S. existing clients are not growing rapidly and the market was dull for the first two quarters.

rows.label: Employee cost run-rate uncertainty
rows.why: Q2 employee cost fell to INR40 crore from INR45 crore in Q1 on about INR1 crore provision reversal and ESOP reversal, and management declined to fix a sustainable run rate while hiring continues.

tone.note: Management was confident on top-line momentum, SciTech and Animal Healthcare, and the 30-32% margin guide, but cautious on the U.S. timeline and deflected analyst questions on deferred sales, employee cost run rate, WELLFA targets and product revenue.
